editorial:
Imagine being a socially awkward teen in a tiny town where nothing ever happens. You will meet Napoleon, a kid with a giant afro and a weird way of talking who spends his time practicing dance moves and arguing with his brother. He is not the most popular guy in school, but he finds a friend in Pedro, a quiet new student who wants to run for class president. The whole vibe of the movie is slow, dry, and wonderfully strange. It feels like you are watching a home movie of the weirdest kids in your hometown, and that is exactly why it works so well.

What really makes this movie stick is the acting; everyone plays their part with a straight face, which makes the jokes even funnier. While the pacing is slow, it fits the mood of a boring small town perfectly. If you love awkward humor and characters that feel like real misfits, you have to see this.
endingExplained: At the big election assembly, Pedro gives a very short and boring speech. Just as it looks like he will lose, Napoleon jumps on stage and performs an amazing dance routine to a synth-pop song. The crowd loves it, and Pedro wins the class presidency. The movie ends with Napoleon finally feeling a bit of success and acceptance, showing that even the weirdest kids can have their moment in the spotlight.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird characters and dry humor.
